title: Mirabel and the Provision
premise: Riverboat captain Astrid Dravenmoor runs cargo on the Greywater, a river that punishes arrogance. When an early tide exposes a sea cave said to hold 'the Provision' — a hoard that grants belonging to whoever claims it — he finds not gold but Mirabel, a fugitive girl carrying proof that the magistrate who rules the river towns murdered her father to seize their trade charter. Hunted by the magistrate's riders and racing the first snows across the Kestrel Range, Astrid must choose between his boat, his freedom, and delivering justice no court will allow. He gets Mirabel and the evidence over the pass at terrible cost — his beloved riverboat burned as a decoy — and in spring, with the charter restored and Mirabel adopted by the riverfolk who owe him everything, he builds a new boat and finally belongs somewhere himself.
about_author: August Ravensworth is the pen name of a former deckhand turned novelist who spent six seasons working inland waterways before trading a tiller for a typewriter. Their fiction is known for rivers that feel like characters and heroes who find family in unlikely places.

chapters.title: The River Keeps Its Books
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A routine run down the Greywater establishes his mastery of the river, his debts to the magistrate's office, and his deliberate loneliness after losing his crew to a rigged inspection. Emotional beat: competent isolation — a man who trusts water more than people.

chapters.title: What the Low Tide Unlocked
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. An unnatural low tide reveals a cave mouth below Widow's Cliff; legends say it holds the Provision. Inside he finds supplies, a hidden skiff — and Mirabel, fifteen, armed with a boat hook and her father's stolen ledger. Emotional beat: wary curiosity hardening into reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: Ink Worth Killing For
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She explains the ledger: Magistrate Corvane forged debt records to strip her father's trade charter, then arranged his drowning. She fled with the only true copy. Riders arrive at the cave; they escape by night skiff. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: Passage Bought in Blood Money
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Corvane posts a reward naming Astrid as accomplice; his old crew abandons him at the dock. He weighs surrendering Mirabel against the one thing the river taught him: you don't leave passengers overboard. They slip upstream toward the Kestrel crossing. Emotional beat: betrayal, then commitment.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Toll
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At Halfway Landing, smuggler queen Odessa Vane offers safe passage in exchange for the ledger — she wants leverage over Corvane too. Mirabel refuses to hand over her father's last truth; Astrid backs her, costing them their guide. Emotional beat: Mirabel learning trust goes both ways.

chapters.title: Riders on the Shale
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Corvane's riders ambush them in the shale canyons; a running fight leaves Astrid wounded and their mule dead. They survive by floating a flooded gorge — the kind of run only Astrid could read. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into fierce partnership.

chapters.title: Snowline
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Above the treeline, the first snows arrive early. Frostbitten and short on food, Mirabel confesses she nearly sold the ledger herself in the night; Astrid admits he almost took Odessa's deal. Honesty binds them like rope. Emotional beat: vulnerability as strength.

chapters.title: The Pass of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The final climb; a storm closes in and riders gain on them. Astrid sends Mirabel ahead with the ledger while he doubles back, burning his own moored riverboat as a decoy fire to mislead the pursuit. Emotional beat: sacrifice — the captain gives up his ship to save his passenger.

chapters.title: Justice Outside Any Court
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Over the pass, Mirabel reaches the free-town assembly at Kestrel Ford and reads the ledger aloud before Corvane's agents can silence her. Odessa, arriving with her smugglers, corroborates with seized records. Corvane's charter collapses; warrants issue. Emotional beat: triumph earned, not given.

chapters.title: New Keel, Old River
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Spring on the Greywater: the charter restored, Mirabel apprenticed to Odessa's fleet and claimed by the riverfolk. Astrid lays the keel of a new boat — named Provision — and lets the town help him build it. Emotional beat: belonging, finally accepted rather than refused.
